title: synchronized versus ReentrantLock
context: How do synchronized and ReentrantLock differ?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Both are reentrant, so the same thread can acquire the lock again. `synchronized` is a language keyword: the lock is released automatically, but you can't try to acquire it with a timeout, it can't be interrupted while waiting, and it has one condition queue. `ReentrantLock` is a class. It offers tryLock with timeout, lockInterruptibly, fairness, and several Condition objects. The cost is that you must unlock in a finally block. Use synchronized for simple cases and ReentrantLock when you need those features.

points.title: Extra features
points.why: ReentrantLock supports tryLock with timeout, interruptible waits, fairness and multiple conditions.

points.title: Always unlock in finally
points.why: A missing unlock on ReentrantLock leaves the lock held forever.
